findings.text: A globally visible updater publishes counter timing and index information into the user mapped page associated with an event when a ring buffer is present, using snapshot derived timing and child aggregate totals.
An overridable weak hook allows architecture code to add platform specific fields to the user mapped page during the update described above; the default does nothing.

A globally visible scheduling hook runs on task switch out, invoking per CPU PMU callbacks when subscribed, emitting switch records when enabled, optimizing clone context switches, and handling cgroup state.
A pair of globally visible subscription routines maintains a per CPU list of PMU contexts requesting scheduling callbacks, with a per CPU usage count reflecting total subscribers.

Slot occupancy is tracked as a distribution over load levels with atomic counters; adding a weight moves one population unit from the old level to the new level and warns on underflow, while merging two distributions returns one plus the highest occupied level or zero when empty.

Pinned task breakpoint load is computed by scanning a hash table keyed by target, filtering by breakpoint category, honoring CPU affinity, weighting each match by its hardware cost, and reporting a sentinel when a CPU wide query meets a CPU affine entry.

Enabling or disabling a breakpoint updates CPU only accounting in per CPU and global structures when no target task exists, otherwise it maintains task accounting with a fast unified path when all task breakpoints are CPU wide and slower per CPU redistribution paths when CPU affine task breakpoints exist or appear or disappear.

Breakpoint validation first delegates to architecture parsing, then rejects kernel space addresses when kernel exclusion is requested, and rejects unprivileged attempts to place breakpoints in the trap path.

Attribute modification requires unchanged event category, supports only the breakpoint category, copies generic signal payload before invoking the category handler, and applies the same steps to the event and each child under the child mutex.

Two scheduling contexts are considered interchangeable for switch optimization only when neither is pinned and when their parent and generation relationships show direct parent child linkage or shared parentage with matching generations.

User page timing is derived from a snapshot clock and context time without the usual context time helper to stay safe in non maskable interrupt context, combining local enabled and running totals with child totals, and adjusting the reported offset by a previous count when the event is currently active.
The reported hardware index is zero when the event is marked stopped or is not in active state, otherwise it comes from the PMU specific index callback.

Statistics synchronization for inheriting events exchanges counter values and swaps enabled and running times between paired old and new events, then refreshes both user pages, applied pairwise over the two context lists.

Event fan out walks either a single task context or both the per CPU sideband list and the current task context, skipping incompletely installed entries and those below inactive state or failing a filter predicate.
Group ordering is defined by ascending group position, implemented as a comparator for a min heap structure.
Slot release derives a category index from the breakpoint type and a hardware cost from the event, then disables the corresponding slot and warns on failure.
One copier propagates breakpoint address, category, length and disabled flag between attribute records, while another propagates only the signal payload during modification.

Stable reads of task pinning histograms require the CPU info semaphore in write mode, while concurrent task slot updates are permitted in read mode; CPU only updates assert write mode and task updates assert read mode plus a constraint mutex.
Scanning the task breakpoint hash table occurs under read side critical section protection with the breakpoint constraint lock asserted for stability.

The fast context swap requires both involved context locks held with nesting and the context disabled, plus absence of no fast switch markers; otherwise the slow path requires the outgoing context lock held while disabling and scheduling out.

User page publication holds a read side critical section for the ring buffer reference and disables preemption for timestamp consistency, bracketing page field updates with an incrementing sequence lock and ordering barriers.
Fan out iteration holds a read side critical section and disables preemption while traversing event lists using read side safe list traversal.
Modification of an event and its children serializes on the child mutex and asserts the absence of a parent context.
Per CPU PMU scheduling callbacks execute with the CPU context locked and the PMU disabled around the callback.

A breakpoint slot moves between enabled and disabled accounting states, with insertion into the task hash on enable and removal on disable for task scoped entries, and with histogram targets chosen by CPU affinity and coexistence of CPU affine entries.

Scheduling out selects between a fast swapped state that preserves hardware programming with exchanged statistics and a slow fully scheduled out state, gated by clone equivalence and no fast switch markers.
Switch notifications are emitted only when switch subscribers exist, with a preemption attribute that is true only for schedulings out of still runnable tasks.
The context scheduling out routine serves as the scheduler invoked entry for optimizing or performing perf context switches during task transitions.
The sideband iterator serves as the entry for broadcasting task switch and similar lifecycle notifications to interested CPU and task events.
Unprivileged breakpoints in kernel trap handling paths risk recursive traps; the validation path mitigates this with a privilege requirement.

Concurrent histogram writers can yield inconsistent snapshots or negative populations; the design requires exclusive stabilization for readers, asserts exclusive ownership during merges, and warns on negative observations.
Invoking blocking or inter processor helpers from the user page path could deadlock in non maskable interrupt context; the implementation avoids that by using snapshot based time derivation.

Observed event state includes a hardware breakpoint target and list linkage, CPU affinity, attribute record, counter and child counter, timing totals and child timing totals, previous hardware count, stopped and active markers, PMU linkage, ring buffer reference, context linkage, and child list with child mutex.
Observed user page fields include a sequence lock, hardware index, counter offset, enabled and running totals, plus architecture extensible tail data supplied with a timestamp.
Observed context state includes a spin lock, pin count, generation and parent linkage, statistic and no fast switch counts, event list, PMU context list, and task association.

Observed breakpoint accounting includes per CPU records holding CPU pinned and task pinned histograms, global histograms for CPU pinned and task pinned per category, and a hash table of task breakpoints keyed by target.
Only the breakpoint event category is accepted for attribute modification; other categories are rejected as unsupported.

Validation and modification signal invalid argument for mismatched type or disallowed kernel address, permission denial for unprivileged trap path breakpoints, and operation not supported for non breakpoint modification.
Visibility and indexing use inactive state as the minimum for notification, active state plus absence of the stopped marker as the requirement for a nonzero hardware index.
